A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments, simulated human decision-making results, and supplementary analyses on Pl@ntNet-300K and iNaturalist-2018.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds RC3P comparison results in Appendix D, Figure 7.

M1.justification: PAS, WPAS, INTERP-Q, and FUZZY retain their scoring functions and procedures. Both holdout and full-conformal reconformalization already appear in v2's appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same full and truncated Pl@ntNet-300K and iNaturalist-2018 datasets, endangered-species setting, and simulated decision-makers. v3's expanded dataset discussion does not introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds rank-calibrated class-conditional conformal prediction, RC3P from Shi et al. (2024), to Figure 7's comparisons on all four dataset variants. v2 cites this method but does not evaluate it. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: The documented splits, validation/calibration allocation, ResNet-50 training budget, metrics, and parameter grids remain unchanged. RC3P joins the existing evaluation setting; newly disclosed calibration-class counts do not establish a change to data splitting.

E4.justification: The FUZZY mapping comparisons, PAS-combination experiments, focal-loss study, species case studies, threshold visualizations, and simulated decision-maker analyses are retained. The added RC3P benchmark comparison introduces no new ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v3 introduces no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds RC3P results, and Appendix D.1 reports inferior size–coverage trade-offs and occasional marginal undercoverage for this comparator. All existing numerical entries in Tables 3 and 4 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a counterexample and proof showing INTERP-Q coverage of (1−α)² for every 0<τ<1 under exact population quantiles. This establishes near-tightness of the existing 1−2α bound through a focused extension of Proposition 3; the other guarantees remain.

C1.justification: The main contributions remain prevalence-adjusted scoring and threshold interpolation for balancing set size and class-conditional coverage on long-tailed data. The revised abstract wording and added discussion recap preserve their scope.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 explicitly clarifies that PAS does not guarantee macro-coverage. Section 2.2 replaces v2's suggestion that INTERP-Q's bound is probably conservative with a near-tight worst-case interpretation. Appendix D.1 also adds explanations for RC3P's difficulties with sparse calibration data.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly reports classes with zero calibration examples: 105 and 606 for full Pl@ntNet and iNaturalist, respectively, and 12 and 47 for their truncated versions. v2 only describes the possibility. Training, hardware, and code-access disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is retained, but Appendix D.1 expands the positioning against RC3P through specific criticisms of its classwise quantile and top-k error estimation, alongside a direct dominance claim for the proposed methods.

P1.justification: v3 adds a labeled objective, clarifies the experimental overview, identifies softmax scoring as LAC, and adds a discussion summary. These accompany localized language edits while retaining the main section and appendix organization.

P2.justification: v3 adopts ICLR title, author, and running-header formatting and reflows existing figures and tables. Figure 7 gains RC3P markers and legend entries, with corresponding axis adjustments; Figure 5 gains 1−α guides and revised legend line styles. The overall display organization remains.

improvement.justification: v3 improves evidential completeness through the RC3P comparison in Figure 7 and replaces speculation about INTERP-Q's bound with a proved population counterexample in Appendix B.3. Clearer coverage qualifications and calibration-data counts improve interpretation and transparency. These are focused gains, with the core algorithms and established experimental results retained.
